## Result
Mode-by-mode cross-walk of BAD-047 PR 1's 13 dbtest cases (test/server/functions.test.mjs:2473-3279) against spike section 2. Wrote no files, ran no tests, did not touch the stack. Verdict: the contract is pinned well — every gate refusal and every fail() body is deepEqual'd on both error and code, join's {allowed:false,reason} shape is pinned including an explicit !('code' in body) at :2487, and the public list row is pinned by sorted key set at :3209. Six looseness findings, one of them material: the suite uses loose assert.equal/deepEqual on JSON bodies, and index.ts:1170/:1191 wrap Postgres bigints in Number() — drop either in the move and scene bytes / saved_at come back as STRINGS while :3248, :3253, :2891, :2896, :2925 and :3242 all still pass. Also loose: :3034 asserts only code on a three-key 413; :2912/:2911/:2662/:2895/:2760 use assert.equal(x, null) which passes for a key that vanished; :2653 and :2964 assert a body with no status; :3230/:3231 substring-match only the sidecar/cam filename while :3229 pins the full member path; :2540 checks status only on report-by-code. Nothing wrong (no assertion contradicts the source). All three ticket cases record rather than endorse (BAD-063 'not the behaviour anyone designed', BAD-064 'the split must not quietly settle on either', BAD-065 'says "too large" for a value that is nothing of the kind') but none cites its ticket number. Gaps: claim/release 403 'wrapping' (only 'closed' tested), join's join_collab/decideJoin refusals other than unknown_code, upload-url 400 bad_collab and missing_digest, 502 storage_unavailable on either signing path, and BAD-065's 'absent bytes' input (the loop sends null, not an omitted key).

## Outcome
Delivered the cross-walk asked for and it held up on spot-check: the two odd shapes (join's {allowed,reason} with no code, fail()'s equal {error,code}) were checked against the source and are correctly pinned, and the six loose assertions it names are real. Its sharpest finding — assert.equal hiding a lost Number() coercion on scene_bytes/saved_at (index.ts:1170,1191) — is the most material thing either child found. One overstatement: it called the BAD-065 loop 'code only' when :3033 does assert the 413 status; the gap there is error and max, not the status.
